root_cause.text: In the vt8500lcd_probe function, the DMA-coherent memory allocated for the frame buffer screen buffer (fbi->fb.screen_buffer) is not freed along error paths after its allocation, leading to a memory leak when probe fails.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new label `failed_free_mem_virt` and a `dma_free_coherent()` call to release the screen buffer, and redirects the failure case of palette allocation (which occurs after screen buffer allocation) to this new label instead of `failed_free_io`, which previously went directly to iounmap without freeing the screen buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement records the physical address of the DMA-coherent buffer. If an error occurs later, this buffer may be leaked because the error path does not free it.
This statement sets the size of the DMA-coherent buffer. Like smem_start, it is part of the allocation that may be leaked on error paths.

This is the assignment of the virtual address of the DMA-coherent screen buffer. After this point, any subsequent error that branches to labels like 'failed_free_palette' will skip freeing this buffer, causing a memory leak as described in the root cause.

This jump statement is an error path that occurs before screen buffer allocation. While it does not directly leak the screen buffer, it is part of the error handling flow that misses cleanup of resources allocated later (like screen buffer) if an error occurs after allocation.

This label is the entry point of an error handler that is reached after partial allocations (e.g., after palette allocation). The handler does not include a free for the DMA-coherent screen buffer, directly causing the memory leak described in the root cause.
